transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
It's election day across the country, and Americans who have not cast early ballots
can go to the polls to cast their votes.
Vermont kicked it off last hour.
Polls have now just opened in Connecticut, Indiana, Kentucky, Maine, New Hampshire, New
Jersey, New York, and Virginia.
Polls will follow in coming hours.
NPR's Stephen Fowler says voters are thinking about unpopular government policies and President
Trump's priorities.
We have polling that say they're concerned about the war in Iran, rising gas prices,
even things that aren't directly economic like corruption, the Epstein files, handling
of immigration.
At the same time, they see the president focus on ballrooms and arches and a reflecting pool.
To be clear, Democrats aren't that popular either, but in many of these places that are
more conservative, those nominees on the left are offering something different than the
Republican Party and the National Democratic Party image.
And we are Stephen Fowler reporting.
In the past few weeks, President Trump has visited or called into rallies of supporters
in more than two dozen states.
For Iran, today's midterm elections may mean a return to war with the U.S. and Israel.
Iran's had its eye on the U.S. elections for months now as part of its pressure campaign
to try to get President Trump to go back to negotiations, and PR's Hadil Al-Shelchi reports.
Iran has used its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway for oil and gas shipping,
to keep gas prices high ahead of the midterm elections, hoping it will anger President
Trump's base and help cost his Republican Party the elections.
While Iran has been defiant, threatening to forcefully retaliate if the war resumes, there's
also been a flurry of visits between Tehran and mediator country Qatar by Gulf and Iranian
officials to try to come to a diplomatic solution.
Iran's foreign ministry has said that they are willing to reopen the Strait of Hormuz
in two days should the U.S. agree to talks.
On Monday, Trump posted on social media that an agreement with Iran "could happen."
Hadil Al-Shelchi, NPR News, Istanbul.
Both Russia and Ukraine say their country's public emergency alert systems were hacked.
NPR's Charles Maines reports.
Ukraine's public air raid app began sending false alerts late Sunday, with varying messages
warning of a chemical weapons attack and high radiation levels, even an incoming strike
by a nuclear-capable missile.
Ukraine's air force quickly assured the public that claims were false and accused Russia
of being behind the stunt.
Meanwhile, on Monday, Russia's emergency situations ministry said one of its alert
systems had been compromised.
Russians received messages claiming the country was under nuclear attack and advising residents
to stock up on food and take cover underground.
Yet the hackers used language not typical of official communiques, a factor officials
in both countries said limited public panic.
Charles Maines, NPR News.
You're listening to NPR.
Two people are believed to have died in Arizona after several days of flooding.
The flooding hit the Four Corners area hard, where Arizona touches Colorado, New Mexico
and Utah.
Some areas got more rain in a day than they do in a month.
Federal investigators say parts of a business jet may have broken off before it crashed
in South Florida on Sunday.
NPR's Joel Rose reports all nine people aboard were killed.
Video recorded by witnesses captured the rapid nosedive and the fiery explosion on impact
near West Palm Beach.
National Transportation Safety Board member Tom Chapman says investigators are trying
to understand why the Learjet crashed on its way from Austin to the Bahamas.
We do have some evidence that there was some breakup of the aircraft before impact.
We're still seeking to determine that.
Chapman says the weather will be a major focus of the investigation, as one of the pilots
reported icy conditions at high altitude moments before the nosedive began.
Multiple media outlets reported that a 20-year-old Florida woman was one of the two pilots, though
NPR has not independently confirmed that.
Joel Rose, NPR News.
The Kennedy Center has named its next class of honorees their songwriter Paul Anka, music
producer David Foster, actor Andy Garcia, playwright David Mamet, and country singer
Barbara Mandrell.
This comes as President Trump has taken control of the nation's Cultural Arts Center and
threatened to demolish the Kennedy Center building if his name is not attached to it.
This year's ceremony will take place at Washington, D.C.'s Capital One Arena, and not the Arts
Center.
It's being renovated.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Election day polls open in Vermont, Connecticut, Indiana, Kentucky, Maine, and other states
NPR's Stephen Fowler reports voters weighing war in Iran, gas prices, and Trump's priorities
Iran uses Strait of Hormuz blockade to pressure Trump ahead of midterm elections
Russia and Ukraine say their public emergency alert systems were hacked with false warnings
Two people believed dead after several days of flooding in Arizona's Four Corners area
Federal investigators say parts of business jet broke off before fatal South Florida crash
Kennedy Center names Paul Anka, David Foster, Andy Garcia, David Mamet, and Barbara Mandrell as honorees
